The Router appropriately marked occluded limbs as untestable rather than guessing. I agree with all `is_testable` and `is_present` judgments. The distinction between Hare and Rabbit is the primary alignment failure.

This is a catastrophic failure for a generation task, as it indicates the model either memorized training data with watermarks or failed to generate a clean image. The 'texture_anomaly' (severity 2) at the ear tips is also valid, showing slight blending issues. The experts confirmed the watermark text is legible (high confidence) but constitutes 'Watermark Pollution'. The pose auditor found minimal structural risk, suggesting the anatomy of the *hare* is correct, even if it's the wrong species.
alignment_reasoning: The image fails the primary class definition. The Fine-Grained Classifier explicitly ranked 'hare' (logit 7.94) far above 'wood rabbit' (logit 2.38). Key morphological features (ear length, body build) contradict the 'cottontail' taxonomy. While the image is a high-quality photo of a hare, it is a misaligned generation for the requested class. Only 3/8 checkpoints were testable and present; 2 testable checkpoints failed due to species mismatch.

This is a critical artifact (Severity 5) indicating data contamination or generation failure. Minor edge haloing on the ears (Severity 2) was also noted. No structural anatomical artifacts (melting/fusion) were found by the pose auditor, but the watermark alone drastically reduces the artifact score.
